شَيِّآنٌ , (K, TA, and L in art. تيح,) in form like the dual of سَيِّدٌ [except as to the final vowel], (TA,) [erroneously written in the CK شَيْئاٰن,]
and شَيَّآنٌ, like تَيِّحَانٌ and تَيَّحَانٌ [q. v.], (L in art. تيح,) [applied to a man,] Far-sighted; (K;) either in the proper sense, or metonymically applied to a man characterized by deliberation, and reflection, and looking to the results of affairs. (TA.) Each is also applied as an epithet to a horse. (L in art. تيح.) [The radical letters of this epithet are either شوأ or شيأ; therefore it is mentioned again in art. شيأ; and another form thereof, without ء, (شَيَّان,) is mentioned in art. شوى.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
